source_text: | DI-001 | `icsp_notebook/kg/eventlog.py` docstring ("design principle 7"); `kg/loader.py` docstring | The append-only event log is the source of truth and the graph is a disposable projection: loading is reset-then-replay and is idempotent. | **inherit.** This is the invariant in `CLAUDE.md` stated as an implementation. |

| DI-002 | `icsp_notebook/kg/graph_backend.py`, `kg/verbs.py`, `tools/verify_neo4j_parity.py` | The seven consumption verbs live once against an abstract `GraphBackend`; Neo4j and NetworkX are two implementations of the same primitives, and parity between them is a gate. | **inherit with adaptation.** The kit mandates one backend-agnostic verb layer and a parity gate whenever a graph runs two projections; the verb list itself is a graph's configuration. |

| DI-003 | `icsp_notebook/docs/runbook_document_admission.md` §4.8 | Derived edges are in the NetworkX build and the export but not in the Neo4j load: "that is the only permitted backend asymmetry, and it is declared, not tolerated." | **inherit.** A declared asymmetry is a configuration entry; an undeclared one is a parity failure. |

| DI-004 | `seldon/docs/seldon_architectural_decisions_updated.md` AD-004 | Each project gets its own database; there is no shared infrastructure, because "Wintermute's LightRAG proved that workspace-based isolation on shared databases is insufficient: different projects contaminate each other's data." | **inherit.** This is why Squiddy is a kit. |

| DI-005 | `icsp_notebook/kg/config.yaml` `neo4j:` block | The projection target database is isolated and named in config: "NEVER wintermute-intake or any seldon-* DB"; credentials come from environment variable NAMES, never values. | **inherit.** The store name and its credentials are graph configuration, and the kit never holds either. |

| DI-006 | `arnold/docs/adr/001-data-layer-separation.md` | Arnold splits Postgres for measurements from Neo4j for relationships. | **inherit with adaptation.** Read as evidence that the store split is a per-graph decision: the kit's invariant does not name a store, exactly as `CLAUDE.md` says. |

| DI-007 | `icsp_notebook/kg/backend_networkx.py` docstring | A NetworkX projection rebuilt from the event log removes the live-driver dependency from every consumer, and it is the path the export and the served copy take. | **inherit with adaptation.** The kit provides a store-free projection as the default; a graph may add a server-backed one. |

| DI-010 | `icsp_notebook/CLAUDE.md` §Standing pointers | "Never a hand edit to the graph or its event log; every change is a logged event." | **inherit.** This is the one forbidden act named in `CLAUDE.md`. |

| DI-011 | `icsp_notebook/docs/runbook_document_admission.md` §11 row "Drift-check both ends" (task `721953b6`, 2026-06-22) | Direct Neo4j writes that are not in the log are invisible to replay and vanish on the next rebuild; the defect was caught by a human reading `build.py`, which is luck and not a control, so `kg/drift_check.py` was built the same day. | **inherit.** The lesson is that the single write path needs a mechanical detector, not a rule. |

| DI-012 | `icsp_notebook/cc_tasks/2026-08-10_c1_ordering_fix_DECISIONS.md` D17 | Log order is semantic: both projections merge with `SET n += props`, so a regenerated slice splices back at the log position the old slice occupied and no event outside the slice moves. | **inherit.** Any regeneration-in-place mechanism the kit offers carries this rule and its test. |

| DI-013 | `icsp_notebook/cc_tasks/2026-07-20_v4_mention_integrity_crosslayer_eval_DECISIONS.md` D2 | Edges that could not be created without rewriting immutable extraction events were created instead by a NEW event type (`mention_resolution`) with a projection branch added to both backends. | **inherit.** Append a new event type; never rewrite an event. |
| DI-014 | `icsp_notebook/corpus/admission_checklist.yaml` B0-snapshot (TEVV safeguard 2, 2026-06-22) | Snapshot the ledger before any write. | **inherit.** |

| DI-015 | `icsp_notebook/docs/runbook_document_admission.md` §4.2 (orphan authority, 2026-06-22) | An incremental append must be scoped to what the increment needs: keeping every idempotent `authority` event from a whole-manifest ingest materialized an orphan `UNECE` node that belonged to a reference-vocabulary entry that is not a Document at all. | **inherit with adaptation.** The kit's rule: a whole-catalog idempotent emitter is a hazard in an incremental write, and the scoped-append filter is a module, not prose. The FSS node labels are configuration. |

| DI-016 | `icsp_notebook/docs/runbook_document_admission.md` §4.2 (v7.4, unit test) | "Scoped to the new doc's agency" is not "no authorities ever": a first document from a new issuer must bring its node with it, or the edge lands on a node the loader cannot match and silently does not exist. | **inherit.** The exception is part of the rule and has to be tested. |

| DI-017 | `icsp_notebook/kg/build.py` `_guard_events_destination` (task `9f853cf9`) | A full-rebuild tool refuses `--only` against the canonical log, because that would delete every other document's events including the stochastic ones it never regenerates. | **inherit.** Destructive-by-design tools refuse their destructive path against the ledger. |

| DI-018 | `arnold/docs/adr/012-effect-verified-writes.md` | No operation reports success until it has observed its own effect; a write that cannot demonstrate its effect by read-back is a failure. Failure behaviour is fail loudly plus quarantine, never rollback fiction, and success responses carry verified counts rather than the word "success". | **inherit.** The largest class in Arnold's 104-bug taxonomy (33 bugs, 32%) is exactly this; the kit's write path returns observed effect. |

| DI-019 | `arnold/docs/adr/012-effect-verified-writes.md` ruling 2 | Where two stores are written, both an in-handler read-back and a scheduled reconciliation sweep are required; the sweep is the standing detector for write paths the handlers do not own. | **inherit with adaptation.** The kit's version is the drift check plus the parity gate (DI-002, DI-040). |

| DI-020 | `icsp_notebook/CLAUDE.md` §Standing pointers; `kg/admission.mk` stage 12 | Zero model calls is the default for every stage of every task; extraction is the only stage that calls a model, and the client is named in config (`kg/models.yaml`). | **inherit.** Stated as a kit rule in `CLAUDE.md`; the client and model policy are graph configuration. |

| DI-021 | `icsp_notebook/kg/admission.mk` header; `docs/adding_a_document.md` §"What this is" | Because the extraction stage is stochastic, this is continuous delivery of an append-only ledger with integrity gates and not continuous integration of a reproducible build: "reproducibility lives at the ledger, not at the extraction." | **inherit.** The kit's reproducibility gate is at the ledger, and it says so. |

| DI-022 | `icsp_notebook/kg/admission_ground.py`; checklist B6-grounding | Every quoted span an extraction records is checked character by character against the source text, and the gate is zero failures; a model that paraphrases, summarizes or invents is caught there and the run stops. | **inherit.** This is what makes a stochastic stage safe to keep. |

| DI-023 | `icsp_notebook/cc_tasks/2026-08-10_v7_3_238g_kill_total_closeout_DECISIONS.md` D35 | Every obligation carries `extractor: {provider, alias, model, date}`, where `model` is the id the client actually resolved and not the alias asked for; the field is ABSENT on legacy records, and that absence is itself the signal that they predate the policy. No backfill. | **inherit.** Recording an alias as if it were the model is the same class of error as citing a document that quotes a statute as if it were the statute. |

| DI-024 | same file, D34 | There is no cross-family fallback: a missing or unauthenticated client HALTS the run with a named systemic error rather than quietly extracting on an unapproved provider. | **inherit with adaptation.** The kit halts on a named systemic error; which providers are approved is the graph's model policy. |

| DI-025 | same file, D35 | A mixed-instrument corpus is accepted: regenerated assertions carry their extractor stamp, legacy ones keep theirs, and a uniformity re-run was explicitly declined as over-engineering. | **inherit.** |

| DI-026 | `icsp_notebook/parked/2026-09-09_reextraction_with_improved_models.md` | Re-extraction with a better model is measure-before-commit: a fixed stratified evaluation sample, a model-rater gold set with adjudication, precision/recall/F1 plus grounding, empty and parse-failure rates and tokens per segment, and a commit rule that B replaces A for FUTURE admissions only if F1 improves without grounding falling. The installed base is re-extracted per document, as logged retire-and-replace events keeping both stamps. | **inherit.** This is the maintenance loop `CLAUDE.md` names; the design is standard information-extraction evaluation and is cited as such. |

| DI-027 | `ai-readiness-kg/docs/research/kg_construction_methodology.md` §2 | "No grounding span, no write." Spans are validated at parse under a declared normalization (NFKC, de-hyphenation, whitespace collapse, case-sensitive, not fuzzy); misses are quarantined at birth; the zero-ungrounded gate is absolute. | **inherit.** The normalization is part of the contract and has to be written down, not implied. |

| DI-028 | same file §2 | The schema whitelist is the only type catalogue; unknown edge types route to a staging area with a `diversion_reason` from a closed list rather than being dropped or admitted. | **inherit.** Neither silent drop nor silent admit. |
| DI-029 | same file §2 | The harness owns provenance: model-emitted ids, timestamps and model names are stripped and re-stamped. | **inherit.** |

| DI-030 | same file §3 | No prompt, profile, model or unit-of-extraction change reaches bulk without a five-document pilot judged against pre-registered thresholds (fabrication share upper bound < 0.10 per stratum at Wilson 95%, item-level faithful >= 0.70, pooled >= 20 admitted items per stratum). A failed gate triggers a new pre-registered pilot, never retuning. | **inherit with adaptation.** The pilot-before-bulk shape is the kit's; the threshold VALUES are a graph's, and these were themselves ported from `fss-policy-kg` realized values. |

| DI-031 | same file §6.1 | Whole-document extraction was an untested design rule and it is wrong: under a large model it produced 108K to 158K-token outputs on three of four pilot documents and doubled per-document cost. The literature predicted the quality effect. The standard is section-bounded, paragraph-integral chunks with a real-tokenizer cap, overlap, breadcrumb context, chunk-local extraction and post-hoc entity resolution. | **inherit with adaptation.** The kit's default extraction unit is a bounded segment, which is what `fss-policy-kg` already does; a graph may override. |

| DI-032 | same file §6.2 | Bulk semantic-edge extraction did not clear the gate and two prompt revisions and a model change did not move it; endpoint co-occurrence near a predicate cue predicts faithfulness at 0.51 to 0.67, which is the distant-supervision false positive (Mintz 2009; Riedel 2010). Disposition: such edges are demand-pull, adjudicated one at a time with the grounding span captured at adjudication. | **inherit.** The kit does not ship a bulk relation extractor, and says why. |

| DI-033 | same file §6.5 | The emission contract, not the extraction unit, is the cost driver: an exhaustive-verbatim contract settled about 2.1x the whole-document arm and quarantined 75.5% of emissions. The revision replaces model-typed quotes with shortest-unique anchors located deterministically by the harness, replaces exhaustiveness with salience plus one gleaning pass, enforces closed lists at parse and reconciles types at merge. | **inherit with adaptation.** The anchor-located-by-harness pattern is a strictly better grounding contract than model-quoted spans and is a candidate for the kit's default. |

| DI-034 | same file §6.6 | A pre-registered precondition (>= 20 items) was inconsistent with a pre-registered threshold (upper bound < 0.10): Wilson 95% puts that bound out of reach below n = 35, so the stratum could only ever fail. | **inherit.** A pre-registered gate is checked for reachability before it is registered. |

| DI-035 | The G4 kill is scoped to Wintermute's Tier-1 bulk extraction instrument and its circuits. It is not a standing constraint on extraction anywhere, and the record says so in consequence 8. | **inherit.** Stated from the record, not from a default reading. |

| DI-036 | What the kill DOES bind: any future graph attempt is a new proposal carrying its own pre-registered gate, decided by that gate and not by argument from the corpse. | **inherit.** This is the kit's own admission ticket; DI-030 is the mechanism. |

| DI-037 | The default reading the task offers is corroborated independently: `fss-policy-kg` ran grounded extraction under Seldon governance after 2026-08-16 (the v7.4 admission of EO 14409, `docs/v74_delivery_report.md`, 2026-09-08, and the v7.10 sweep that admitted two OMB memoranda on 2026-09-10). No gate treated the kill as binding on it, and nothing in the kill record says it should have. | **inherit.** Recorded so the question is not reopened from the ambiguity it does not have. |

| DI-038 | `T1_INDEX` was archived, not deleted: 21,758 nodes marked `state: killed_g4` **by event**, append-only history preserved, no graph deletions. | **inherit.** A kill is a logged state transition, which is the same mechanism as a supersession. |

| DI-039 | `ai-readiness-kg` reached the same disposition independently for its semantic edge stratum and cites G4 by name (`kg_construction_methodology.md` §6.2: "Disposition, same as Wintermute G4"). | **inherit.** Two builds, one finding: bulk relation extraction without per-edge adjudication does not pass a faithfulness gate. |

| DI-040 | `icsp_notebook/kg/drift_check.py` docstring; checklist B1/B10 | One verdict over two legs: the manifest equals the log, and the log replayed equals the live graph. The manifest leg is offline and runs first, so an outage still proves half and says which half it proved. | **inherit.** The reproducibility gate `CLAUDE.md` mandates, in its tested form. |

| DI-041 | `icsp_notebook/cc_tasks/2026-08-10_c1_ordering_fix_DECISIONS.md` D18 | `prov_wasGeneratedBy` is the one field a regeneration may change: the drift gate excludes it from the semantic diff and then SEPARATELY asserts that it is the only field that ever differs, which is strictly stronger than a blanket exclusion. | **inherit.** The pattern generalizes to any exclusion in any diff. |

| DI-042 | `seldon/docs/seldon_architectural_decisions_updated.md` AD-006 | Every quantitative result is a first-class artifact with a provenance chain to the script, the data and the requirement; "if a number doesn't exist in the registry with status >= verified, the system should flag citation attempts." | **inherit with adaptation.** Seldon owns research results; the kit owns graph assertions, and the shape is the same. |

| DI-043 | `icsp_notebook/kg/derive_edges.py`; runbook §4.8 | Derived edges are a deterministic build-time projection, tagged `derived=true` and method-versioned; two runs over the same raw state produce byte-identical output. | **inherit.** Derived is a declared class, never mixed with raw. |

| DI-044 | `icsp_notebook/kg/grading_layer.py` (task `e1e22a0d`, D3) | A grade is a provenance-tagged ADJUDICATION attached to the structure, never a graph axiom. | **inherit.** Judgment is recorded as judgment. |

| DI-045 | `icsp_notebook/kg/conflict_reversibility_check.py` | An overlay claim is verified by a FILTERED REPLAY excluding that capability's activity ids, which must reproduce the pre-overlay projection exactly. | **inherit.** An overlay that cannot be replayed away is not an overlay. |

| DI-046 | `icsp_notebook/docs/runbook_document_admission.md` §5 (v7.4) | Where a layer cannot hold a fact, the fact is a logged ABSTENTION with a reason code (`kg/implements_abstentions.jsonl`, `kg/reference_abstentions.jsonl`, reason `target_not_a_document`), never a silent omission. | **inherit.** "An edge or a logged abstention, never neither." |

| DI-047 | `icsp_notebook/docs/v72_closeout_delivery_report.md` §Part C | "An empty CONFLICTS_WITH result is not evidence that definitions are reconciled": an overlay answers only the question it adjudicates. | **inherit.** Absence in one layer is not evidence in another; the same rule the fsskg MCP server states for its concept layer. |

| DI-050 | `icsp_notebook/docs/runbook_document_admission.md` §3; `kg/manifest_ingest.py` docstring | Currency status is parsed deterministically into supersession edges from a listed set of phrasings, and free prose that matches no pattern SILENTLY produces no edge. | **inherit with adaptation.** Inherit the deterministic parse; adapt the failure mode. Silence here cost three months of a served status the catalog denied (v7.7), so the kit fails loud on an unparsed status rather than emitting nothing. |

| DI-051 | same, §14 (v7.7) | An express rescission and a lapsed authority are the same edge and not the same fact: where the status is a judgment rather than a quotation, the mechanism says so (`supersedes in substance`, `mechanism: supersedes_in_substance`) and the whole reasoning goes in the notes, so a later reader can overturn it on evidence. | **inherit.** Writing a rescission the source does not state, to make a parser emit an edge, would put a false quotation in the catalog. |

| DI-052 | same, §14; `tests/test_supersedes_catalog_target.py` | A supersession target that is cataloged rather than admitted broke both backends differently on the same log: Neo4j wrote nothing and NetworkX created a phantom node. | **inherit.** Edge endpoints resolve across the whole inventory, not only the admitted part, and the two projections are tested for agreement on it. |

| DI-053 | `icsp_notebook/kg/extent_retirement.py`; `kg/fr_extent_retire.py` | Retirement withdraws content from the PROJECTION while the event log keeps every event, and the retirement itself is an appended event that predicts its projection delta before anything is written. | **inherit.** This is how the kit removes without deleting. |

| DI-054 | `~/.wintermute/docs/decisions/2026-08-16_g4-kill-consequences.md` consequence 4 | A kill is a logged state transition on the affected nodes, with append-only history preserved and no deletions. | **inherit.** Same mechanism as DI-053, at a larger scope. |

| DI-055 | `seldon/docs/design/AD-017_central_validity_ontology.md` | The shared ontology is one master and many read-only replicas synced by a monotonic epoch counter; replicas cannot be modified locally, write protection is enforced in `create_artifact`/`update_artifact`, and master-assigned UUIDs are copied verbatim so references work across the boundary. | **inherit.** The identity spine, and the only shared thing in a federated design. |

| DI-056 | `sfv-paper/paper/glossary.md` T4; `paper/sections/07_operationalization.md` | State Supersession Failure: a decision is explicitly revised but the old value persists in operative state. The prescribed countermeasure is a revision log with versioned entries and validation of each use point against the current revision; the indicator is the parameter revision propagation rate. | **inherit with adaptation.** The kit's ledger IS the revision log; the adaptation is that "each use point" for a graph means each projection and each served surface. |

| DI-060 | `icsp_notebook/docs/runbook_document_admission.md` §10 | A name is a property and a key is an identifier: the key never changes on either path. A name changed by executive action becomes surface forms plus a currency note; a name changed by statute becomes a logged rename with the enacting instrument as provenance. Never a hand edit. | **inherit.** The general form: an identity change is a logged event carrying the authority that made it. |

| DI-061 | `icsp_notebook/cc_tasks/2026-08-10_v7_3_238g_kill_total_closeout_DECISIONS.md` D40; `kg/resegment.py` | Segment ids are CONTENT-ADDRESSED, not positional: a segment is matched to its old id by exact equality on a normalized form, so changing one block's classification churns that block's id and nothing else. An estimate of 989 stranded obligations measured as zero. | **inherit.** Content-addressed unit identity is what makes re-segmentation affordable, and the kit's units carry it by construction. |

| DI-062 | `arnold/docs/adr/016-exercise-id-convention.md` | Opaque numeric ids imported from a source are unreadable at the point of use and caused a real misidentification; the census that settled it found the opaque namespace about 97% orphan and the log path already assuming readable ids. | **inherit with adaptation.** The kit's default id is a readable, source-scoped slug; a graph may pin an external identifier as its spine (the first consumer pins DOI and OpenAlex). |

| DI-063 | `ai-readiness-kg/docs/research/2026-08-23_tgbench_shacl_report.md` §Export counts | Extracted item ids are document-scoped and 600 of 6,988 distinct ids recur across documents, so a projection that MERGEs on the bare id fuses same-id items from different documents into one node. The RDF export deliberately scopes the IRI by document and records the fusion as a finding against the other projection. | **inherit.** Id scope is a kit-level decision and has to be stated once, or two projections of one ledger disagree. |

| DI-064 | `~/.wintermute/docs/2026-07-28_labnote_canonicalization-decision-and-er-literature.md` §5 D1 | Duplicate entities are collapsed by ALIAS-TO-CANONICAL with recoverable un-merge, never by physical merge. Ruled on merits: every KG operated at scale for a decade converged on redirect with exercised un-merge; this graph already paid the destructive-merge price (29,918 edges copied, 29,552 recovered, 366 orphans unrecoverable pending review). | **inherit.** Irreversible merge is forbidden in the kit; the reversible overlay is the mechanism. |

| DI-065 | same, §4 | Entity resolution is a named field with a standard decomposition, cited rather than re-derived: normalize, block/index, pairwise classification under Fellegi-Sunter's three-zone rule (link / non-link / clerical), cluster with cluster-level validation rather than naive transitive closure over sameAs (Halpin et al. 2010), survivorship/canonical election with everything else an alias, predicate canonicalization (Galarraga et al. 2014; CESI 2018), and B-cubed cluster-level evaluation. | **inherit with adaptation.** The kit does not ship an entity resolver. It ships the decomposition's vocabulary and the constraint that a resolver is a separable, gated, reversible overlay. |

| DI-066 | same, §4 item 4; `~/.wintermute/docs/2026-06-08_labnote_machine_era_kg_entity_resolution.md` (cited there) | High neighbour overlap is bivalent: it means both "should merge" and "must never merge", so a homonym gate must precede merge eligibility, and negative evidence (`NOT_SAME_AS`) is a hard constraint. | **inherit.** Recorded so the kit never ships a similarity-only merge. |

| DI-070 | `icsp_notebook/CLAUDE.md` §"The manifest is the inventory control system" | The manifest is the authoritative list of what is and is not in the graph; there is no other entry point and no other record. Every document ever considered has exactly one entry, every action on a document is a change to that entry first, and a declined entry carries the reason, the metadata and what would change the decision. **Declined is a decision, not a backlog.** | **inherit.** This is the kit's inventory control system, stated in `CLAUDE.md` already. |

| DI-071 | same | Nothing enters the graph without a manifest entry saying it is admitted, nothing is in the graph the manifest does not say is in it, and disagreement between them is a gate failure rather than a footnote. | **inherit.** DI-040's manifest leg is the mechanism. |

| DI-072 | `icsp_notebook/docs/runbook_document_admission.md` §1 (v7.5) | Rejection has a reason code (`excluded:out_of_scope`, or `excluded:deferred` when a NAMED condition would flip it): without one, "assessed and declined" and "nobody looked" are the same state, which is exactly what an absence question cannot afford. | **inherit.** |

| DI-073 | same, §3; `corpus/manifest_schema.md` | Status is a two-axis profile of existing standards rather than one invented enum: `stage` profiles UNECE GSBPM, `disposition` profiles DDI-Lifecycle. | **inherit with adaptation.** The two-axis shape is the kit's; the vocabularies are configurable, and a graph that has no GSBPM analogue supplies its own. |

| DI-074 | same, §1 | The admission criterion is a reference-resolution test, not topical adjacency: a document is admitted when it resolves a dangling definitional or authority reference from a document already in the corpus. Three bases exist, each naming the evidence it requires, and each entry states its basis verbatim AND which halves it does not satisfy. | **inherit with adaptation.** The criterion's SHAPE (a mechanical test against evidence in the graph, an explicit statement of what it does not prove) is generic. The three bases are FSS-specific and are a graph's assessment criterion. |

| DI-075 | same, §1 (v7.5) | Do not build a vocabulary-overlap metric to decide membership: it was tried and measured, and it scored a pure-quantum executive order above the AI one, because it measures that a document is a federal executive order, not that it belongs. | **inherit.** Recorded so nobody re-derives it: similarity is not admissibility. |

| DI-076 | same, §1 (v7.7); `corpus/layers.yaml` | A scoped layer needs a scoping record written BEFORE the admission, carrying five parts: why the record exists (the admission declined for want of it), measured evidence that the layer already exists, a membership rule a task can apply against text, **the exclusions** (the working half; a rule with no exclusion clause admits its publisher's whole output), and the boundary the record does not cross. | **inherit with adaptation.** Generic shape, FSS content. `corpus/layers.yaml` is the machine-readable form and is a model for the kit's configuration. |

| DI-077 | same, §14 (v7.7) | Currency is decided against the corpus BEFORE it is decided against a sweep: a query for the id in the graph (a citation edge, a supersession status, a correction note) is stronger evidence than anything a fresh external sweep produces, and it is free. | **inherit.** The in-corpus check runs first and costs nothing. |

| DI-078 | `icsp_notebook/docs/v710_delivery_report.md` §Reported, not fixed item 2; `kg/config.yaml` `admission:` | The manifest said `in_graph` from the moment the criterion admitted, which is before ingestion; a run stopping between stage 1 and stage 6 leaves the catalog claiming an ingestion that never happened. v7.11 added an `admitting` state and a measured abandonment threshold (30 minutes, five times the longer of two measured end-to-end runs). | **inherit.** The kit's manifest carries an in-flight state, and the threshold is measured rather than chosen. |

| DI-079 | `icsp_notebook/docs/v74_delivery_report.md` and `v75_delivery_report.md` §Reported, not fixed item 1 | `kg/manifest_ingest.py` emits a document event for EVERY manifest entry regardless of stage or disposition, so "cataloged, not ingested" is enforced by the scoped append and not by the code; a full rebuild would materialize nine non-admitted entries as documents. Reported across three arcs and not fixed inside an admission. | **inherit as a defect not to repeat.** The kit's catalog emitter filters on stage, and a rebuild is tested against the same expectation as an increment. |

| DI-080 | `icsp_notebook/CLAUDE.md` §Standing pointers; `squiddy/CLAUDE.md` | The corpus is 100% public: a document goes in only if a program can fetch it from a public source with no login, no payment and no restrictive licence, and one that cannot is declined with the reason recorded, never left as a to-do for the operator. | **inherit with adaptation.** Public-only is a per-graph policy recorded in the manifest metadata, and the assessment stage enforces whatever the graph declares. |

| DI-090 | `icsp_notebook/kg/admission.mk` header; `kg/stage.py` | The pipeline is a dependency graph in which each stage is a rule, A GATE IS A RULE WHOSE OUTPUT FILE EXISTS ONLY ON PASS, and the stage record is the rule's output. A failed gate leaves no target, so it is re-attempted and nothing downstream can be satisfied by it. The pattern is cited to ODK's Makefile-driven builds and ROBOT's `report`/`verify`, not invented. | **inherit.** This is the kit's execution model. |

| DI-091 | `icsp_notebook/docs/adding_a_document.md` §"Where the checks come from"; runbook §11 | Every check started as a defect; none was invented in advance and none is hand-curated taste. Each stage records the report and the date of the defect that created it, and "a gate you cannot name an incident for is a gate someone will skip." | **inherit.** Stated in `CLAUDE.md` already; the stage manifest is where it is carried. |

| DI-092 | `icsp_notebook/kg/canary.py`; stages 9 and 10 | Predict the delta BEFORE the change and check it after: "a table written after the fact records what happened, a table written before it is a claim that can be wrong", and it has been wrong. | **inherit.** The ordering is the whole value. |

| DI-093 | `icsp_notebook/cc_tasks/2026-08-10_c1_ordering_fix_DECISIONS.md` D17; checklist B7-c1 | A drift gate is a PROPERTY DIFF, not a count: the broken run reported a plausible 808 to 818 concept count while 383 concepts were overwritten and 88 lost surface forms. A count is exactly what hid it. | **inherit.** |

| DI-094 | `icsp_notebook/docs/runbook_document_admission.md` §11 ("the 111-node phantom") | Discover labels and relationship types from both sides and compare the union; never enumerate them. A gate whose coverage depends on someone remembering to extend a tuple goes stale on exactly the run that adds a layer. | **inherit.** |

| DI-095 | same, §6.3 and checklist D2-oracle | A pinned oracle is not a tunable: it is bumped deliberately, in the same commit as the regenerated artifact, with a comment reconciling the delta stage by stage against a snapshot that reproduces the prior numbers exactly. - **Squiddy is a system of systems, not a monolith.** Finding, fetching and screening documents is a separate
  component: working name **Tentacle**, the operator's choice of name stays open.

- **The interface is the input wall** (DN-028). Tentacle hands Squiddy a candidate manifest and the files: identifier
  or path, provenance, retrieval status with reasons, and screening verdicts. Squiddy builds the graph from it.

- **Tentacle's model is the PRISMA 2020 flow** (Page et al., BMJ 2021). Identification is by source: databases,
  registers, local shelves, citation lists. Then duplicates removed, records screened and excluded, full texts sought
  and not retrieved (with reasons), full texts assessed and excluded (with reasons), included. Every stage carries in
  counts, out counts and reasons.

- **Why separate.** Squiddy was proven on one easy corpus (library: open-access papers with DOIs). Arnold exposed
  every dimension where intake differs: books, scans, access rules, breadth of scope. A framework is not general
  until it has served about three different applications (Roberts and Johnson, "Three Examples").
- No Tentacle work, and no new intake rules in Squiddy, until Arnold passes end to end (KG-004).

- Then one design review maps rules R-147 to R-166 onto the PRISMA stages, moves what belongs to Tentacle, deletes
  duplicates, and adds a permanent fixture set of hard intake cases: scan, EPUB, title-only first page, paywalled DOI,
  PMID-only citation, PMC-only paper, publisher 403, the same file in two folders.

## R-01 A kit, not a system

Squiddy is a library, a skill and templates that each graph instantiates locally. It never stores
content and never runs as a service. Evidence: Wintermute's monolith drift, diagnosed by the
operator on 2026-09-10 as "ingest machinery centralized while the design said distributed, so
content followed the only pipeline that existed" (DI-004). Prior art: OBO Foundry ODK and ROBOT
(Jackson et al. 2019; Matentzoglu et al. 2022), Monarch's LinkML/KGX/Koza/KG-Hub stack, Seldon
AD-002 (domain-agnostic engine, domain configuration as schema).

## R-02 Extract, do not design

The kit's first version is `icsp_notebook`'s `kg/admit.py` spine with FSS-specific parts factored
to configuration. Rule of three satisfied (fss-policy-kg, AI-readiness KG, Wintermute, and
ai-readiness-kg as the fourth per S-001). Measured by S-001: 88% of stages and 94% of spine lines
generic or parameterizable. Failure mode avoided: Brooks's second-system effect.

## R-03 No rewrite to RDF/OWL

Property graph and JSONL ledger stay. LinkML is the schema language on top; ontology identifiers
are referenced by CURIE, never copied. Evidence: the biomedical graphs the operator half-recalled
as "the OWL paradigm" are property graphs on Neo4j with formal schemas (Hetionet, Himmelstein et
al. 2017; SPOKE, Morris et al. 2023; Biolink, Unni et al. 2022; BioCypher, Lobentanzer et al.
2023). The OWL lives in the vocabularies, not the store.

## R-05 Candidate kits: measure before adopting

Pre-registered rule (adopt / harvest components / reject), applied in S-001. Result: no candidate
passes adopt; LinkML adopted for schema, KGX for interchange, BioCypher / Koza / ODK / ROBOT harvest
components, TrustGraph and Neo4j LLM Graph Builder rejected (TrustGraph's components already
harvested 2026-08-23 in ai-readiness-kg). The BioCypher spike is not triggered.

## R-06 LinkML ratified at corrected scope

S-003 measured: the "1,565-line dual projection" was two files, not the duplication. Removable
with the schema: 489 of 821 projection lines (60%). Not removable by any schema: the
event-to-instance transform (217 lines, written once, Koza's layer) and store semantics (115
lines). The parity gate becomes two writers over one instance stream plus schema validation at
export, because two LinkML generators disagreed on one slot in the same run.

## R-07 First consumer is the bibliographic evidence graph; Arnold is second

Bounded to what the kit's recorded decisions cite plus the standards they rest on; public
metadata, abstracts, open-access text only; DOI and OpenAlex as its identity spine. Reasons: entity
resolution nearly solved by external authorities; abundant schema prior art (CiTO, FaBiO, schema.org
ScholarlyArticle); it eats its own dog food. Arnold's domain (clinical vocabularies, a person as an
entity, wearable time series) is the hardest kind and should meet a kit already proven. This
disagrees with the Arnold thread's proposal and is the ruling.

## R-08 The manifest is the inventory control system for every graph

One entry per document ever considered (cataloged, held, admitted, declined with reason and
metadata); nothing enters a graph except through it; manifest-vs-graph disagreement is a gate
failure. Public-only is a per-graph policy the manifest declares and the assessment stage
enforces. Inherited from fss-policy-kg's 2026-09-10 rule (DI-070, DI-071).

## R-09 Identity spine: local mint, registry election, bridge by record (OD-4 defaults stand)

S-004's five assumptions accepted without an override window, per the doctrine (decide, state,
proceed): A1 the registry elects an existing id and mints nothing; A2 it is a zero-content Squiddy
graph beside seldon-ontology, not inside it; A3 `exactMatch` only on declared authority key
equality or a human ruling, everything probabilistic is `closeMatch` and non-transitive (SKOS
Reference 2009); A4 query-time lookup serves recorded bridges and decides nothing (Translator
NodeNorm); A5 the Work is the unit, DOIs identify expressions (FRBR; DI-152). Evidence and prior
art in `docs/OD-4_identity_spine.md` §7 (31 sources). The operator overrides by naming the letter.

## R-10 Maintenance is scheduled stages with gates, never unbounded agents

Currency, drift, dedup, and the measure-before-commit re-extraction loop (parked design in
icsp_notebook) run as scheduled pipeline stages. The weekly sweep is the template; Wintermute's
OODA self-healer is the counterexample.

## R-11 Secrets and API keys

Credentials live in `.env` at the repo root, gitignored, with a committed `.env.example` naming
every variable and none of the values. The kit's acquire stage reads `OPENALEX_API_KEY` (and any
other authority credential) from the environment through one accessor, never from config files,
never logged, never written into a manifest, a report, or an event. Absent a key, the stage runs
in the public pool and records `auth: none` on the run. The operator has an OpenAlex key and adds
it to `.env` himself; no task asks for it, prints it, or moves it.

## R-12 Budget is never a target

Unused weekly quota is not spent on extraction ahead of a manifest, a schema, or a pipeline. The
first consumer reaches the acceptance bar with zero model calls by design (its first assertions
are deterministic from public sources).

## R-13 After the ask is met, stop

Recorded because it was violated on icsp_notebook on 2026-09-10 (arcs dispatched by mining

## R-15 Four things, one truth

A Squiddy graph is four things. Only one of them is the record.

| # | thing | what it is | lifetime | in git | how it is made |
|--:|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Ledger** `events.jsonl` | Append-only, immutable event log. Every assertion, retraction, ruling and admission, in order, with provenance. **The source of truth and the audit record.** | Permanent | Yes, tracked (DI-001; the icsp gitignore says why: E3 events are stochastic and not regenerable) | The single write path appends; nothing else touches it (DI-010) |
| 2 | **NetworkX projection** | In-memory graph rebuilt from the ledger by reset-then-replay (about one second on fss-policy-kg). Runs the gates, the drift check, the export and the parity check without a live driver (DI-007). | One process | No; it is never written to disk as itself | Replay of #1 |
| 3 | **Neo4j database** | The live projection you query, explore and serve MCP verbs from. One database per graph, database name = graph name (DI-004, DI-005). | Long-lived but disposable: reset-then-replay from #1 reproduces it exactly, and the drift check proves it (DI-040) | No | Replay of #1 |
| 4 | **Export** (node-link JSON, versioned) | Release artifact: portable copy, deployment copy where Neo4j is unavailable (the HF Space), input to the release diff. One row per version in the register (DI-110). | Kept on disk per the register; regenerable | No (35 MB per copy on fss-policy-kg; churn) | Written from #2 |

Ledger-as-truth is the ruling for every graph Squiddy builds. R-04 left "which store is truth" per
graph; this note closes that for Squiddy graphs. Reason: Neo4j writes are `MERGE` and `SET n +=`,
which overwrite; an overwritten value leaves no record of what it replaced. The audit evidence
State Fidelity Validity requires (an immutable record plus the recorded process that reproduces
every derived state) can only be the ledger. Neo4j is where you work; the ledger is what you can
prove. A write to Neo4j that did not go through the ledger vanishes on the next rebuild and is a
drift-check failure, not a feature (DI-011).

## R-16 The ledger is segmented, because the record is the thing that grows

Measured 2026-09-13: `icsp_notebook/kg/events.jsonl` is 64,273,858 bytes, tracked in git. GitHub
warns at 50 MB and refuses at 100 MB. fss-policy-kg is already past the warning.

Prior art: every event-sourced store segments its log (Kafka log segments; EventStoreDB chunk
files; Fowler's Event Sourcing pattern with snapshots). The kit's form: one immutable ledger file
per release (`ledger/<release>.jsonl`), sealed when the release is cut, plus an index file naming
the segments in order and each one's sha256. Replay reads the segments in index order. A sealed
segment is never appended to. No single file grows past a bound, git diffs are per release, and a
segment's hash in the register is its integrity check. Git LFS is rejected: pointers break plain
`git diff` and every clone has to fetch blobs it may never replay.

Whether the kit already writes under the release marker in a way that makes this a rename or a
change is measured in S-009 before anything is written; the FSS ledger is not touched (locked for
the deliverable).

## R-18 Continuous improvement is a scheduled, bounded, receipted stage

The operator's intent: when there is capacity, sample a hundred claims, correct what fails spec,
record who reviewed each and what changed, and the graph is a hundred claims better.

The form that intent takes is fixed by R-10 and R-12. "We have spare cycles, go improve the graph"
is the trigger that produced Wintermute's self-healer (DI-137) and the R-13 violation on
icsp_notebook; it is refused as a trigger. The same work as a stage is correct:

- **Audit sweep stage.** Sample n claims by sha256 order of claim id (the S-007 rule), n fixed in
  the graph's config, rated against the fixed rubric; every verdict a `Ruling` node with
  `RulesOn`; corrections written as retract-and-append events, never edits (DI-013, DI-053).
  Registers per run: claims sampled, share failing, share corrected, tokens. Scheduled on a
  cadence (the weekly sweep template), never by capacity.
- **Reviewer provenance.** The `Ruling` schema gains `agent_kind: model | human` and `agent`: the
  resolved model id (DI-023) or the human's name. A human review is a ruling like any other;
  it is never a gate (DI-098). The audit sweep's consumer (T-7) is the served `status` on each
  claim, which every verb already returns.
- **Re-extraction loop.** When a prompt, model or segment rule changes, the measure-before-commit
  loop (DI-026): fixed stratified sample, model-rater gold set with adjudication, commit rule
  "B replaces A for future admissions only if the rater line improves without grounding falling",
  installed base re-extracted per document as logged retire-and-replace.
- **Cross-graph dedup and currency** are stages of the same shape, scheduled, gated, receipted.

## R-19 Design before build, because the ledger is append-only

The operator asked for the waterfall shape: high agreement on the first stage and the best
available picture of the later ones before any build. Royce (1970), whom the word is credited to,
argued the single pass fails and drew the feedback loops; what has changed is the cost of a loop,
not the cost of a design error. In this system a design error is the expensive kind: schema and
invariant mistakes propagate into an immutable ledger and are corrected by logged retraction, not
erased. So the front-loaded stage is schema, invariants, gates and vocabulary; everything
stochastic runs behind a pilot; and the feedback loop is the pre-registered gate that fails, which
is cheap because it was designed to be. Agreement on the plan is recorded as the proposed tasks
below; a build thread executes them and does not redesign them.

## R-20 The prefix is everything in the call that is not segment or output

H-004's parent file defines the fixed prefix as "instruction plus schema". Two registered results
contradict that reading. HV-008 finding 2: 5,340 mean metered tokens per extractor call, about 490
of it the paper text and the prompt together, the rest CLI per-call scaffolding and side models.
S-007 pilot: 1,327 input tokens per invocation to a Haiku side call the CLI makes itself. The
instruction is therefore the small part, and a task that measured only it would confirm a
breakdown nobody disputes while leaving the 5k unexplained. Part A reports the call by component
(CLI default system prompt, built-in tool definitions, MCP tool definitions, memory injection,
environment block, instruction plus schema, segment, output, side calls), each registered.

Consequence: H-004 Part C (a shorter instruction) is skipped by its own 2,000-token condition when
that condition is read against the instruction's row. Halving 490 tokens cannot move a 5k prefix.

## R-21 A fourth remedy: minimal-scaffold invocation, compared under the same rules

Remedy 1 converts prefix creation into prefix reads. Removing the prefix is the other half of the
design space and H-004 did not list it. Prior art: `takelushi/claude-code-rs` (tested against CLI
v2.1.94) ships it as the default configuration, stated purpose "to reduce unnecessary context sent
to the CLI": no session persistence, empty setting sources, strict and empty MCP config, no
built-in tools, no slash commands, the caller's text as the entire system prompt. Anthropic's CLI
reference documents `--system-prompt` as replacing the default prompt and a `--bare` mode. Same
client and same auth, so R-11 holds. Flags are verified against the installed CLI's help, never
recalled.

It is compared, not adopted: it changes what the model sees, so claims ratio (at or above 0.85 of
baseline) and per-paper grounding (at or above 0.95) are real tests, exactly as for H-002's
batching, which saved 6.7x and was refused. It runs before Remedy 1 because a prefix diff is
cheaper on a small prefix and because prompt caching has a model-specific minimum cacheable
length: below it Remedy 1 has nothing to act on and the two do not combine.

One rate limit, one prompt-cache namespace, one ledger. A cache-read share measured while a second
process issues near-identical prefixes is contaminated in the direction of the hypothesis under
test. And the 100M ceiling does not refund tokens spent at the baseline rate while a cheaper
transport is hours from a verdict: at 600k per hour against a baseline projection near 330M, the

## R-23 The SessionStart hook is unrecorded process, which the invariant forbids

H-004 found a user-level `SessionStart` hook injecting a 2,799-token skills preamble into all 3,235
extraction calls. CLAUDE.md's invariant: every derived state reproducible from primary sources plus
the recorded process. Text from `~/.claude` that reaches the extractor and appears in no record is
process that was not recorded. A re-run on another machine, or on this one after the hook changes,
is a different extractor under the same version string. So `--setting-sources ""` is owed on
reproducibility grounds whatever the cost comparison says, and the existing claims need the hook's
text hashed and attached to their runs by an appended event while that text is still recoverable.

This does NOT adopt Remedy 4. The per-paper grounding floor refused it and that verdict stays on
the record. R-23 says why the question must be re-asked properly, and R-24 says how.

## R-24 A refused arm is re-tested on unseen papers against a threshold that predates every arm

Rules 12.3's floor (0.95 per paper, not pooled) has no noise term. `findings_acl_972` sits at
exactly 0.9500 in the baseline, so a second baseline run would fail its own floor on roughly half
of attempts; the rule cannot tell an arm from a replicate on that paper. Prior art: non-inferiority
designs state a margin and a confidence bound before the data (Piaggio et al. 2012, CONSORT
extension; FDA 2016 guidance); A/A runs measure what a comparison calls a difference when none
exists (Kohavi, Tang and Xu 2020, ch. 19); Newcombe 1998 for the interval on a difference of
proportions. S-012 already carries the same defect for the rater gate (Wilson bound).

The frame, fixed here before any call:
- Verdict papers: the 15 pilot papers no remedy arm has touched. The five H-002 papers are reported
  beside them and excluded from the verdict, because they are the data that prompted this ruling.
- Lines: the daemon's own pilot gate, in config since S-007 and older than every arm. Pooled
  grounding at or above 0.98; schema validity at or above 0.98; GROUNDED claims at or above 0.85 of
  the baseline's grounded claims on the same 15 (ungrounded claims never reach the ledger, so yield
  of grounded claims is the quantity that matters). Newcombe 95 percent interval on the grounding
  difference reported, not gated.
- Noise: one replicate of the arm on the five seen papers, giving an A/A pair per paper. Reported.

The objection is DI-174's and is recorded rather than answered away: this frame was written after
seeing an arm fail the old one. What separates it from a moved threshold is that the verdict rests
on papers no arm has seen and on lines nobody chose for this comparison.

Three candidates change what the CLI does around the extractor and nothing the extractor reads:

and `--bare` are the documented candidates), prompt-cache writes that are never read
(`DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING`; H-004 notes the writes are the 1-hour kind, priced at 2x, against a

## R-28 Value is concept coverage with diminishing returns, because the citation layer cannot rank

R-26 ordered by citation events per token. H-005 found every work carries the same citation value,
so the ratio collapsed to shortest-first: a rule nobody chose, which buys the 535 shortest works
and leaves the 293 longest unread. The mention layer HV-009 released gives each work a concept set
before any model call (15,219 edges, 4,167 concepts). With a budget and sets, this is budgeted
maximum coverage (Khuller, Moss and Naor 1999); DN-005's first draft named it and was wrong to
retreat to the knapsack reading.

Plain coverage pays only for the first work on a concept, and S-013 needs the opposite: two claims
from different works on one concept before a contradiction candidate can exist. So the value of
adding a work is the sum over its concepts of 1/(k+1), k being the works already chosen that cover
that concept. That function is monotone submodular; greedy by marginal value per token holds a
constant-factor guarantee under a knapsack constraint (Nemhauser, Wolsey and Fisher 1978;
Sviridenko 2004). Recomputed at each paper boundary, zero model calls. First, measure why the
citation layer is flat (its distribution), because a flat value layer is either a fact about the
corpus or a defect in the citation parse, and the second is Issue 8e888b61's open condition (3).

## R-32 The control chart of R-29 is withdrawn; the threat it watched is now closed by construction

H-006 built the chart to DN-006's specification and it failed its negative control: 54 of 288
papers signal, paper 21's profile among them. The specification was wrong in two places, both
Desktop's. Limits of 3 sigma over root n treat calls as exchangeable across papers, and they are
not: the variation between papers dwarfs the variation within one, the case the three-way chart
exists for (Wheeler, Understanding Statistical Process Control, ch. 9; Montgomery section 6.4 on
rational subgroups). And the statistic subtracted segment tokens estimated at one corpus-wide 2.98
characters per token, so each paper's own tokenization ratio landed in the "fixed" residual. CC
refused to install it, correctly.

It is not rebuilt. What it was for was the fixed part of a call growing unseen. Since H-005 and
H-006 that part can change only through a config edit: setting sources are off and checked by the
stage, the binary is pinned and verified at start, and a new version is a new pilot. A detective
control over something preventive controls already hold is cost without a threat. The per-paper
intercept of presented tokens on segment characters (the fixed cost with the paper's own
tokenization taken out) is logged as a number on each paper and gates nothing. `chart.enabled`
stays false and the block says why.

## R-33 Find what restarts the daemon, and checkpoint by segment before the long documents arrive

daemon.log shows a new run id at 09:53:53Z and 10:46:40Z on 2026-09-20, each about 40 seconds into

## R-34 Test-retest reliability of the extractor is measured before anything downstream leans on claim identity

H-005's A/A pair moved claim COUNTS by at most one per paper. H-006 Part D then found 330 of 1,326
baseline claims with no overlapping candidate claim in the same segment, 215 candidate-only, 184 of
those re-selections, spread evenly over papers (Gini 0.29) and positions. So the 8.7 percent yield
gap has no kind to it and no instruction remedy is indicated: R-31 closes there. What it opened is
larger. Counts agree while a quarter of claim identities do not, across arms. Whether that is the
arm or the extractor's own run-to-run variation is unmeasured, and the A/A pair that answers it
already exists on five papers. Zero model calls: match claims between the two replicates by segment
and span overlap, report the share of claims with a counterpart, per paper and pooled, with the
same matcher H-006 Part D used so the numbers are comparable.

Prior art: test-retest reliability (the term and the design are a century old in measurement);
span-matched agreement as in MUC and CoNLL evaluation, exact and partial; Krippendorff's alpha for
unitized data where the units themselves vary between coders (Krippendorff 2013, ch. 12), which is
this case exactly. The consequence, if the replicate share is near the cross-arm share: a claims
graph is one draw from a distribution, S-013's contradiction candidates inherit that, and the
remedy space (k-run intersection, self-consistency voting as in Wang et al. 2022) is a design
session and not a patch.

## R-36 The oracle labels already exist, so the cascade is calibrated at zero model calls

BARGAIN calibrates on a few hundred oracle labels. This run holds one per segment for 520
documents: every call's status says whether the extractor found a grounded claim there. That is
tens of thousands of labels, free. The proxy is trained and its threshold calibrated on them,
split BY DOCUMENT (a segment-level split leaks a document's vocabulary across the line).

## R-37 The proxy is local. A cheap model tier is not cheap in this client

The literature's second tier is a small LLM. Here a call costs about 1,000 tokens before the
segment is read (H-004, H-005), so a Haiku pre-check would cost what it saves. Tiers: (0)
deterministic code, for segments that are structurally not prose: reference lists, tables of
contents, indexes, acknowledgments, numeric tables, fragments under a length floor; (1) a linear
classifier on lexical features, trained on R-36's labels, run locally. Anything heavier is
justified by measurement against tier 1 or not added.

## R-38 Quality is the constraint and cost is the objective

Pre-registered before any fit: minimize calls subject to retaining at or above 0.98 of GROUNDED
CLAIMS (claim-weighted, not segment-weighted: a skipped segment holding four claims costs four) on
held-out documents, with failure probability 0.05 by BARGAIN's recall-target procedure. Checked
separately within each document-size quartile and within the documents over 500,000 characters
already extracted, because a threshold that holds on papers and fails on books is the failure the
operator's hypothesis predicts. If no threshold saves at or above 20 percent of calls at that
recall, adopt nothing and say so.

Two things bound the claim. The labels are one draw from an extractor whose test-retest agreement
H-007 Part C is measuring; recall against a noisy oracle is recall against that draw, and the
report says so with H-007's number beside it. And a skip is recorded, never silent (R-23): the
record carries the tier, the score, the threshold and the classifier's hash, so every skipped
segment is recoverable by a later run and nothing about adoption is irreversible.

## R-39 The operator's hypothesis is measured, and the science joins the corpus

Grounded claims per 1,000 characters against document length and document kind, over the 520
extracted: zero model calls, reported whatever it shows. The works above are admitted through the
corpus's own admission path, the same one every other work came through; if that path takes only
thread citations, this note and this conversation are the citation.

`kg_construction_methodology.md` is copied into `docs/` here with its source commit recorded, and

## R-41 Packs with harness-located anchors are tested now, because that is where the money is

A squiddy call is about 1,000 fixed tokens carrying about 200 tokens of segment: over 80 percent
overhead. The cascade of DN-008 can remove at most the share of calls that find nothing. Packing
removes the overhead itself: at 1,500 tokens of text per call the fixed part falls to about 40
percent, roughly 3x on every remaining document, and it composes with the cascade.

H-002 tried 1,000-token batches, measured a 6.7x saving, and refused them on grounding (0.866 and
0.889 against 0.95). ai-readiness-kg's chunked arm PASSED its faithfulness gate at the same unit
size (F_upper 0.0458, item-faithful 1.000). The visible difference is 6.5's anchor contract:
there the harness locates a short unique anchor; here the model types the span and the harness
checks it, and typed spans drift as inputs lengthen. Hypothesis, not mechanism: H-002's grounding
loss was the emission contract, not the unit. One arm tests it: section-bounded paragraph packs,
cap 1,500 real tokens, breadcrumb, anchors located by the harness, against DN-005 R-24's frame
(pooled grounding and schema validity at or above 0.98, grounded claims at or above 0.85 of the
per-segment protocol's, on documents no arm has seen), with H-007's test-retest share beside it.
Overlap is omitted on purpose: packs are paragraph-integral, claims here are sentence-local, and
overlap would double-extract; if boundary loss shows in the claims ratio, that is the finding.

6.5's 33-46K-token outputs are not this pipeline's problem: output here is about 6 percent of a
call. 6.2 concerns typed relations; squiddy extracts claims, not relation triples, so its gate
evidence stands as measured here. Prior art sets the first hypothesis. It does not replace the

## R-43 Claim quality is entailment, coverage and decontextualization, measured before any protocol is called best

The instrument is ai-readiness-kg's probe protocol, ported not rebuilt, extended by Claimify's two
other dimensions with its published judging prompts as the starting point. Raters are not the
extractor. It is positive-controlled before any verdict is read (methodology 7.6): planted
non-entailed claims, planted claims with unresolved referents, and a planted pack with its
verifiable sentences withheld must each be caught at or above 0.9.

## R-44 One bake-off, three arms, quality as the constraint and cost as the objective

Same 15 already-extracted documents, stratified by size, seeded draw, none touched by any earlier
arm:
- **A, per-segment (current).** Existing records; zero extraction cost.
- **B, packs with anchors** (DN-009 R-41): 1,500-token paragraph-integral packs, breadcrumb,
  harness-located anchors.
- **C, B plus the Claimify contract in one call:** the instruction asks for verifiable assertions
  only (selection), each rewritten to stand alone using the breadcrumb and the pack, added context
  in square brackets as Claimify marks it, one assertion per claim; anchor unchanged.

Pre-registered rule. FLOORS, per arm, on a seeded sample of 150 claims and 100 source sentences:
entailment by ai-readiness-kg's thresholds (F_upper < 0.10, item-faithful at or above 0.70);
anchor grounding at or above 0.98; schema validity at or above 0.98. Among arms clearing the
floors, rank by USABLE CLAIMS PER MILLION TOKENS, a usable claim being entailed AND decontextualized
AND grounded, and require sentence-level coverage at or above 0.90 of the best arm's so a sparse
cheap arm cannot win on price. Every arm's full row is reported so the operator can overrule the
ranking with the numbers in front of him. No fourth arm and no re-registration without him
(anti-spiral clause).

## R-45 What follows from the verdict is decided now, not after

If B or C wins: it becomes the protocol for the 320 remaining documents, records carry `unit` and
`emission`, and the report prices re-extracting the 530 already done at the winning arm's cost
against A's measured decontextualization rate, so the operator sees one number for a homogeneous
graph. If A wins: resume as it was, and the week's cost work stands as the answer. The cascade
(DN-008) is fitted afterwards at the winning unit; H-008 and its addendum are superseded by H-009,
which keeps their zero-call measurements. A gleaning pass is tested only if the winner's coverage
is under 0.85, because in this client it doubles the cost.

## R-46 One call runner; everything that calls a model or the network goes through it

`squiddy` gets a single runner for repeated external calls. It owns: the unit key (hash of arm or
stage, item id, rater or role, prompt hash, model, transport); the append-only fsynced JSONL
checkpoint; resume by skip; progress every 60 seconds or N units to stdout and a log; the pilot
(default 20 units or 1 percent) that prints projected tokens and wall clock and records them
before continuing; token and wall-clock ceilings from config that stop new calls, let in-flight
ones land, and exit non-zero; failures as rows under a bounded retry; aggregation over whatever
the checkpoint holds, stating n. The daemon's extraction loop, the quality instrument's raters and
scorer, corpus fetches and every future harness use it. The meter and the token bucket sit inside
it, so a call cannot be unmetered either.

## R-47 The stage fails code that goes around the runner

A static check over the package and `scripts/`: any invocation of the model client, `subprocess`
to the CLI, or an HTTP library outside the runner module fails the build, with a planted
violation as its positive control (DN-003 T-2). One kill test per consumer of the runner: SIGKILL
mid-loop, restart, final output equals an uninterrupted run's, no completed key called twice.
Tests use a stub client; they cost nothing.
